source_title: Pawan Khera Explains INDIA Bloc’s Mock Parliament Plan for Public Impeachment of CEC Gyanesh Kumar - India Today - India Today
source_excerpt:
Congress Media Chairperson Pawan Khera stated that the INDIA bloc will enact a mock Parliament session to conduct a public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Speaking at 10 Rajaji Marg, Khera said the mock proceedings will be attended by opposition Members of Parliament and civil society representatives. He explained that the event had to be shifted to Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence lawn as a last resort because permissions were denied at Ashoka Hotel and police stopped them from unloading equipment at Ramlila Maidan. Khera asserted that the event articulates the nation's aspirations ahead of the November 1 rally. Read More

Political Row Over Tata Battle: Rahul Gandhi Attacks Modi Govt, Nirmala Sitharaman Hits Back
The corporate battle for control of the Tata Group has triggered a sharp political confrontation between the opposition and the government. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi accused the Modi government of attempting to destroy Tata to help corporate allies take over, drawing a sharp response from Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, who defended the government's support for entrepreneurs and accused the Congress of spreading toxicity. The face-off follows Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata challenging the reappointment of N. Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons Chairman, citing procedural lapses at a board meeting. Nationalist Congress Party leader Sharad Pawar had earlier voiced support for Noel Tata as the boardroom struggle heads towards the courts.
SC on Delhi SIR: Logical Discrepancy Scrutiny, Voter Roll Objections & Form 6 Row
The Supreme Court has made critical observations while hearing petitions concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Delhi. The court noted that it has not yet adjudicated on the legality of the 'logical discrepancy' category, which previously led to the deletion of 27 lakh voter names in Bengal as an interim measure. Addressing the ongoing process in Delhi, the bench questioned why individuals excluded from draft rolls are being directed to submit Form 6 instead of Form 8 for address changes. The court observed that time to submit claims and objections must be extended before the rolls are finalised, highlighting ongoing legal concerns surrounding the voter revision exercises across different states.
Face Off: Dr Nishant Anand and Tuhin Sinha debate MLC election outcomes
A debate on India Today's Face Off examines the political outcomes and implications of legislative council elections across four key states. Dr Nishant Anand, National Spokesperson of the Congress, confronts Bharatiya Janata Party National Spokesperson Tuhin Sinha over seat losses in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Maharashtra. Dr Anand emphasizes that the ruling dispensation lost in prime constituencies including Varanasi, Patna, and Pune, arguing the outcome reflects public dissatisfaction while pressing demands for conducting future elections via paper ballots. In response, Tuhin Sinha defends the Bharatiya Janata Party, pointing out that the party secured 14 out of the 21 seats it contested, including a complete sweep in Karnataka, whilst the Congress drew a blank across all contested seats. Sinha dismisses allegations regarding electronic voting machines as an excuse for repeated electoral failures, maintaining that the Bharatiya Janata Party regularly introspects on narrow margins and localized anti-incumbency across long-held strongholds.
MLC Poll Setback: NDA Sweeps Karnataka 4-0 as Congress Draws Blank Across States
The Congress party faced a major electoral reverse in the Legislative Council elections across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar, failing to win a single seat. In Karnataka, the opposition BJP-JD(S) alliance swept all four seats on offer, with the BJP retaining three seats and JD(S) winning the Bengaluru Teachers seat against five-time Congress MLC Puttanna. The elections were conducted using paper ballots rather than Electronic Voting Machines. The NDA targeted the Congress over the outcome, noting that the ruling party failed to secure victory even on ballot papers amid its campaign alleging vote theft. Opposition parties also registered gains in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, while Congress acknowledged the defeat and indicated plans to review results.
